graph_operations.observation: If the message's node already exists, the transformer retains and updates its graph entry while choosing a parent from available message, existing-node and fallback data.
If absent, it creates a mapping entry with message, parent and child information and marks the node as new.
Parent selection considers an existing node, the message's parent metadata, fallback identity, author type and a special merged-message-fragment continuation condition.
On an accepted parent, the transformer adds the child reference if missing and repairs obsolete links to a previous parent where needed.
A parent-chain traversal is used to avoid some invalid fallback ancestry and to identify a descendant relationship before relinking.
If a proposed new parent lies beneath the node in the old ancestry, the transformer can rotate a descendant relationship and adjust related parent/child links, reporting the rotation.
The calling state writer conditionally preserves or changes currentNode using preserve-current-turn intent, new-node status, rotation results, and selected ancestry relationships.
The state writer can update locally optimistic prompt state for the affected message or parent before publishing the new conversation state.

The state writer constructs updated conversation state with the new mapping/current selection, sends it through a local state helper, and returns the message ID, parent ID, previous state and next state.

The conversation state commit updates a visible-message projection. For a changed node it attempts an incremental projection update; otherwise it can recompute the visible selected path from the mapping and current node.

When selected-node or relevant parent information changes, the state commit may walk the current-node parent chain, gather user-author messages in root-to-leaf order, and update a separate user-ancestry projection. The walk guards repeated identities.

structural_guarantees_visible_in_code: Reciprocal parent/child rewrites are attempted when a node changes parent.
New child references are checked for existing membership before insertion.
Ancestry and rotation logic can prevent or repair some inconsistent local graphs.
The selected current node is decided by a separate caller rather than always choosing the inserted message.
The update result exposes old/new conversation state to further local processing.
not_verified: No proof that every input graph is valid or that all cases preserve global acyclicity.
No proof of server-side message ancestry implementation or the exact export data format.
No proof that the live client exercised any specific conditional insertion or rotation.
The final component selectors, render subscriptions and reactivity triggers consuming these projected state fields remain untraced.
privacy: Capture-local semantic roles and original analytic summaries only; no source code, IDs, network endpoints, filenames, routes or user messages.

state_commit_observation.client_behavior: The scoped conversation commit explicitly updates a message mapping, selected node, selected-path visible-message cache, and conditional user-ancestry list, alongside request status and other client fields.
state_commit_observation.verification_boundary: These are saved client state-set operations; how individual UI components subscribe and render remains a separate source-tracing task.
